newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka probe reveals plot against president.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka probe reveals plot against president.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state media said an influential former minister, arrested under the country's emergency laws last week, was being investigated over an alleged plot to kill President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
The state-owned Daily News said on Sunday that police had uncovered information about the plot and were investigating further.

State television said late on Saturday that Sirisena Cooray, a minister in the former United National Party (UNP) government who was arrested on unspecified charges, was being grilled about a possible assassination attempt on Kumaratunga.

Police officials were not immediately available for comment, but the independent Sunday Times quoted Criminal Investigation Department chief T.V. Sumanasekera as saying there was some information on the plot and investigations were continuing.
Cooray's lawyer, Hemantha Waranakulasuriya, told Reuters on Sunday: "It's a pack of lies. The government has not made a single statement implicating Mr Cooray in an assassination attempt.
"We intend to sue Rupavahini (state-run television) and the Daily News for this," he added.
Cooray was arrested on orders of the Defence Ministry and is being held in a government house in Colombo.
On Friday, police detained another opposition politician, U.L. Seneviratne, a provincial council member of the opposition UNP.
Seneviratne was a close confidant of assassinated president Ranasinghe Premadasa, and Cooray was a minister in his cabinet.
Both men can be held for up to three months under emergency laws, which are usually used against people seen as a threat to national security.
On Thursday, a hearing by the Supreme Court on Cooray's arrest was postponed because the attorney-general was absent.

Cooray, who returned to the island in April after a long stay abroad, has been ordered to appear before two presidential commissions probing poll malpractices and the killing of a senior UNP politician in 1993.
The UNP's 17-year reign ended in 1994 when Kumaratunga's People's Alliance won power.
